sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Why assumptions need their own mechanism
sections.what: Explains the purpose of the file, the three kinds of objection a critic can raise, and the three ways an assumption can be resolved. It also sets up the imports for the enum and the assumption record.
sections.why: The docstring explains that a written reply to a missing-evidence objection can be accepted without the design changing, so a typed resolution is required.
sections.watch_out: The mechanism only works if the typed fields stay strict. Loosening them lets a prose disclaimer stand in for a real resolution.

sections.name: AssumptionResolution
sections.title: The three possible outcomes
sections.what: Lists the three outcomes for a named assumption: grounded, because evidence was found; declared prerequisite, because it is true but needs something to land first; and unsupported, because nothing establishes it.
sections.why: The docstring says a fourth outcome, meaning under investigation, was considered and rejected. That state would absorb every inconvenient assumption at no cost.
sections.watch_out: Adding a fourth outcome would reopen the escape route the docstring describes, so the list is intentionally closed.

sections.name: DeclaredAssumption (part 1)
sections.title: The assumption record
sections.what: Defines one assumption with its statement, its resolution, its evidence ids, an optional prerequisite kind and reference, and an optional reference to the claim that prompted it. The record is frozen and rejects unknown fields.
sections.why: The docstring says a reassurance is not a resolution, so the statement must be specific enough to test.
sections.watch_out: A vague statement such as the systems can be integrated cannot be tested, so it works as a caveat rather than a check.

sections.name: DeclaredAssumption: _check_resolution_is_backed
sections.title: Checking that each resolution is honest
sections.what: Checks that the chosen resolution matches its fields. Grounded needs cited evidence. Unsupported must cite none. A declared prerequisite needs a named, typed prerequisite and cited evidence. Any other resolution must not name a prerequisite. A separate read-only property reports whether an assumption counts as an unresolved gap.
sections.why: The code's messages say each resolution must be what it claims to be, otherwise the claim refutes itself or avoids the coverage penalty that unsupported carries.
sections.watch_out: A mismatch raises an error when the record is built, so the record is rejected and never reaches the planner. Check the error text before editing the rule.

summary: Defines the record for an assumption that a future-state design depends on, and forces each resolution to be backed by the right typed evidence or prerequisite.
purpose: Stops an unproven assumption from being hidden behind a reassuring sentence, so the design either has evidence, a named prerequisite, or an honest unsupported label.
why: The module docstring explains that some objections are about missing things rather than wrong citations, and a written reply can satisfy a critic without changing the design. A typed field cannot be satisfied with prose.
how: Defines three resolution values: grounded, declared prerequisite, and unsupported. Then defines the assumption record with a statement, a resolution, evidence ids, an optional prerequisite kind and reference, and an optional reference to the claim that prompted it. A validation step checks that the resolution matches the fields. A read-only property reports whether an assumption is an unresolved gap that counts against coverage.
inputs: Assumption records from the architect stage, including evidence ids and any prerequisite name and kind.
outputs: Validated assumption records, or a validation error that explains the mismatch. The gap property returns true or false.
risks: Loosening a check so a declared prerequisite passes with no evidence. Naming a prerequisite under a resolution that does not create an ordering constraint. Writing a statement too vague to test.
debug: Read the validation error text, which names the assumption and the broken rule. If the gap count looks wrong, check the resolution value on each assumption, because only unsupported ones count as gaps.
